correctness.rationale: For each rank t, domain and image block-index sets are disjoint exactly when the partial injection squares to empty; the order constraint fixes their pairing and the t local permutations contribute (m!)^t. Direct enumeration independently verifies all 17 small configurations. For fixed m, the factorial weight is precisely the law of iid ternary labels conditional on zero signed sum; lattice local CLT and a binomial-tightness argument prove the normal limit and sharp square-zero fraction. In the factorial-critical regime the exact neighboring-vacancy ratios converge to parity-Poisson terms under a summable majorant, yielding total-variation convergence. Finite experiments do not replace either proof.

originality.rationale: The 2019 primary article defines the whole block inverse-monoid family and counts all elements but does not derive the square-zero block-rank census or the factorial-scale parity-conditioned Poisson transition in its inspected Sections 1–3. The 1994 and 2015 nilpotent literature concerns ordinary (unblocked) monotone partial injections and/or all nilpotents; those related cases are credited rather than represented as new. The generalized-central-trinomial count is known as a coefficient identity, but no inspected comparison supplies the full algebra-specific two-parameter asymptotic statement. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not proof of publication priority.
residual_risks: Full 1994 Garba and 2015 Laradji–Umar original texts could not be read; a prior equivalent or dominating result cannot be ruled out.
The exact count is a generalized central trinomial coefficient; a general published asymptotic coefficient theorem may already imply the factorial-critical limit.

The fixed-m Gaussian limit follows classical conditional multinomial theory; the originality judgment concerns its precise monoid realization and two-regime factorial-scale transition, not the probabilistic tool itself.

value.rationale: The family is a natural block-permutation extension of ordinary monotone partial injections, with two meaningful independent size parameters. A rank-resolved square-zero census determines a structural invariant, and its factorial-scale transition between O(k) Gaussian vacancies and O(1) parity-constrained Poisson vacancies identifies when almost-maximal square-zero block rank becomes typical. The precisely parity-dependent double limit and sharp full-monoid probability provide information absent from scalar size/presentation results; mere trinomial-coefficient re-expression is not counted as the contribution.
